source_text:
Homilia 9
Ἀστερίου ἐπισκόπου Ἀμασείας εἰς τὸν ἅγιον τοῦ Χριστοῦ μάρτυρα
Φωκᾶν
9.116 Ἱερὸς μὲν καὶ θεσπεσίος ἅπας ὁ τῶν γενναίων μαρτύρων κατάλογος, πάθει τὴν
ὑπὲρ πάθους ἀποδοὺς χάριν, αἵματι δὲ τὴν ὑπὲρ αἵματος τῷ Σωτῆρι τῶν ὅλων
ἀμοιβὴν ἐκπληρώσας. Πλὴν ἐν αὐτοῖς τούτοις οὐ μία τῶν πάντων ἡ δόξα, οὐδὲ πρὸς
ἓν μέτρον ἴσα τὰ γέρα τοῖς ὅλοις ἀπο κεκλήρωται, ἀλλὰ τὸ πρῶτον καὶ δεύτερον
οὐδὲ ὁ τῶν ἁγίων ἐκφεύγει κατάλογος. Αἴτιον δὲ οἶμαι τούτου τὸ λίαν
ἀπηκριβώμενον τοῦ κριτοῦ καὶ ἀπρόσκλιτον. Ἐφορᾷ γὰρ καὶ τιμωριῶν μεγέθη καὶ
καρτερίας ἐνστάσεις, καὶ βασανίζων τὸ ἀγώνισμα τὰς πρὸς ἀξίαν ἀμοιβὰς διανέμει
τοῖς ἀθληταῖς. Καὶ παράδοξον οὐδαμῶς εἰ παρὰ Θεοῦ οὕτως τιμᾶται τὸ δίκαιον,
ὁπότε καὶ παρ' ἡμῖν στρατηγοὶ καὶ ἀγωνοθέται οὐκ ἴσοι γίνονται τοῖς ἀριστεῦσιν ἢ
τοῖς ἀγωνισταῖς, ἀλλὰ δὴ ἑκάστῳ κατὰ τὸ μέτρον τοῦ κατορθώματος τὰς δωρεὰς
ἀναλογούσας ἐπιψηφίζουσιν. Ταῦτα δὲ διῆλθον, ἵνα δείξω ὡς ὁ σήμερον ἡμῖν
παρασχὼν τοῦ συλ λόγου τὴν ἀφορμὴν τῶν ἑταίρων καὶ συναγωνιστῶν ἐστι
περιφανέστερος. Οἱ μὲν γὰρ ἄλλοι οὔτε πάντες παρὰ πᾶσι γνωρίζονται, οὔτε
βεβοημένην ἔχουσι τὴν ἀνδραγαθίαν· Φωκᾶν δὲ οὐκ ἔστιν ὃς ἀγνοεῖ· ἀλλ' ὥσπερ ἡ
ἀκτὶς τοῦ ἡλίου πᾶσιν ὀφθαλμοῖς ἐφήπλωται, οὕτω καὶ ἡ τοῦ μάρτυρος τούτου
φήμη πᾶσαν ἀκοὴν περιήχησεν· εὐθὺς γὰρ ἐν τῷ τιμίῳ τούτου σήκῳ γενόμενος καὶ
τῇ ἱερᾷ θήκῃ τοῦ σώματος προσψαύων ἐκ τοῦ τόπου πληροῦμαι τῆς μνήμης πάντων
ὁμοῦ τῶν ἐπ' αὐτῷ λεγομένων διηγημάτων· βλέπω τὸν κηπουρὸν τὸ ἐπιτήδευμα, τὸ
ἄπλαστον τῆς 9.118 ψυχῆς, τὸ φιλόξενον, τὸν τῆς παραλίας ἐξαίρετον, τὸν τῆς
μεσογείας εὐεργέτην, καὶ μαθητὴς μάρτυρος γίνομαι μανθάνων ἄχρι τῶν ἐσχάτων
κινδύνων φυλάττειν τὴν εὐσέβειαν. Ἀλλὰ γάρ, εἰ δοκεῖ, τῶν κοινῶν καὶ πολλοῖς
γνωρίμων ἀφέμενος τὰ ἐξαίρετα τοῦ μάρτυρος διηγήματα ὑμῖν τοῖς φιλομάρτυσι
διηγήσομαι. Ἤνεγκε τὸν ἅγιον ἄνδρα τοῦτον, τὸ μέγα χριστιανῶν ὄφελος, ἡ γείτων
Σινώπη, πόλις ἀρχαία καὶ γνώριμος, εὔπορος γενναίων καὶ φιλοσόφων ἀνδρῶν.
Ἐπιτήδευμα δὲ αὐτῷ τοῦ βίου κήπου γεωργία καὶ ἐπιμέλεια, ὅνπερ αὐτοῦ που πρὸ
τῆς πύλης τοῦ ἄστεος ἐπὶ τοῦ στόματος τοῦ Ἰσθμοῦ κεκτημένος ἤσκει φιλοπόνως,
ἑαυτῷ καὶ τοῖς δεομένοις παραμυθίαν τοῦ βίου. Ἤνοιγε δὲ καὶ τοῖς ξένοις μάλα
προθύμως τὴν μικρὰν καὶ πενο μένην ἑστίαν. Ἐποικῶν δὲ τῇ λεωφόρῳ κοινὰ τοῖς
ἐπιδημοῦσι προετίθει τὰ ὄντα· καὶ νέος ὢν Λώτ, οὐ Σοδομιτῶν, ἀλλὰ Σινωπέων. Τοῦ
χρόνου προελθόντος τὴν ἐντολὴν εὗρεν οὐκ ἄμισθον· ἀπὸ γὰρ τῆς φιλοξενίας
ἐκέρδανε τοῦ ζωοποιοῦ θανάτου τὴν πρόφασιν· ὅθεν δὲ καὶ ὅπως μικρὸν
ἀναλαβόντος ἀκούσατε. Τοῦ λόγου τῆς εὐσεβείας ἡμῶν καταγγελθέντος καὶ τοῦ
θαυμασίου κηρύγματος πρὸς πᾶσαν ἀκοὴν ἐξελθόντος, γνωρίζοντος δὲ τὸν Χριστὸν
καὶ τὰ ἀπ' ἐκείνου μυστήρια, ἐφρυάξαντο ἔθνη, κατὰ τὸν ψαλμῳδόν, καὶ οἱ βασιλεῖς
καὶ οἱ ἄρχοντες συνήγοντο ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό· καὶ οἱ τῆς πλάνης λαοὶ ὠργίζοντο τοῦ Ἰησοῦ
βασιλεύσαντος. Ἐζητεῖτο δὲ πᾶς χριστιανὸς ὡς κακοῦργος καὶ ὁ ἐγγὺς ἐκολάζετο καὶ
ὁ μακρὰν ἀνιχνεύετο. ∆ιὸ καὶ Φωκᾶν οὔτε ἡ εὐτέλεια τοῦ ἐπιτηδεύματος καὶ ὁ
κηπουρὸς ἔκρυψεν, ἀλλὰ καὶ οὗτος ὡς γνήσιος τοῦ Χριστοῦ μύστης ἐμηνύθη. Καὶ δὴ
καὶ ἦλθον ἐπ' αὐτὸν οἱ τοῦ δυστήνου τοῦδε βίου καὶ ῥέοντος κελευσθέντες
thought_title: All martyrs holy, but Phocas surpasses them
orientation: Asterius, bishop of Amasea, opens his homily on the martyr Phocas by explaining that even among holy martyrs there are degrees of honor, and Phocas is among the most renowned.
pass_a_gloss: Holy indeed and divine is the whole catalog of the noble martyrs, having given back by suffering the grace on behalf of suffering, and by blood having fulfilled the reward on behalf of blood to the Savior of all. But among these very ones the glory of all is not one, nor have equal honors been allotted to all by one measure, but the first and second place does not escape even the catalog of the saints. And the cause of this, I think, is the very exact and impartial judgment of the judge. For he oversees both the magnitudes of punishments and the instances of endurance, and testing the contest he distributes the rewards according to worth to the athletes. And it is not at all paradoxical if by God justice is thus honored, since also among us generals and contest judges do not become equal to the bravest or to the contestants, but indeed to each according to the measure of the success they vote the corresponding gifts. And these things I have gone through, in order that I may show that the one who today has provided us the occasion of the assembly is more distinguished than his companions and fellow contestants. For the others are neither all known by all, nor do they have their courage loudly proclaimed; but Phocas there is no one who does not know; but just as the ray of the sun is spread over all eyes, so also the fame of this martyr has sounded around every ear; for immediately when I have come into this honored shrine of his and touch the sacred receptacle of the body, from the place I am filled with the memory of all the stories told about him at once; I see the gardener, the occupation, the unfeigned quality of the soul, the hospitality, the exceptional one of the coast, the benefactor of the inland region, and I become a disciple of the martyr, learning to keep devotion even to the last dangers. But indeed, if it seems good, leaving aside the common and widely known things, I will narrate to you, the martyr-loving ones, the exceptional stories of the martyr. This holy man, the great benefit of Christians, neighboring Sinope bore, an ancient and well-known city, rich in noble and philosophical men. And his occupation of life was the cultivation and care of a garden, which he possessed somewhere there before the gate of the city on the mouth of the Isthmus, and worked it laboriously, as a comfort of life for himself and for those in need. And he opened to strangers very eagerly his small and poor hearth. And dwelling by the highway he set before the visitors his possessions as common; and being a new Lot, not of the Sodomites, but of the Sinopeans. As time went on he found the commandment not unrewarded; for from hospitality he gained the occasion of the life-giving death; and whence and how, listen, taking up the story a little. When the word of our devotion had been proclaimed and the wondrous preaching had gone out to every ear, and made known Christ and the mysteries from him, the nations raged, according to the psalmist, and the kings and the rulers gathered together to the same place; and the peoples of error were angry at Jesus having become king. And every Christian was sought as a criminal, and the one near was punished and the one far off was tracked down. Therefore neither the cheapness of the occupation nor the gardener hid Phocas, but he too was denounced as a genuine initiate of Christ. And indeed there came upon him those who had been ordered by the ones of this wretched and fleeting life.

choices.term: Ἱερὸς μὲν καὶ θεσπεσίος ἅπας ὁ τῶν γενναίων μαρτύρων κατάλογος
choices.english: Holy indeed and divine is the whole catalog of the noble martyrs
choices.why: Keeps the μὲν...δὲ structure visible and renders κατάλογος literally as 'catalog' to preserve the list imagery.
rejected: Holy and divine is every list of noble martyrs
The whole list of noble martyrs is holy and divine

choices.term: πάθει τὴν ὑπὲρ πάθους ἀποδοὺς χάριν
choices.english: having given back by suffering the grace on behalf of suffering
choices.why: Preserves the dative of means (πάθει) and the reciprocal 'on behalf of' (ὑπέρ) structure, which is central to the rhetorical balance.
rejected: having returned grace for suffering through passion

choices.term: τὸ λίαν ἀπηκριβώμενον τοῦ κριτοῦ καὶ ἀπρόσκλιτον
choices.english: the very exact and impartial judgment of the judge
choices.why: Renders the articular infinitive phrase as a noun phrase and keeps both adjectives as attributes of the judgment, matching the Greek word order.
rejected: the judge's extreme exactness and impartiality
the very precise and unbiased nature of the judge

choices.why: Directly echoes the Psalm wording (LXX Ps 2:1) and keeps the aorist middle force.

choices.term: οἱ τοῦ δυστήνου τοῦδε βίου καὶ ῥέοντος κελευσθέντες
choices.english: those who had been ordered by the ones of this wretched and fleeting life
choices.why: Makes clear that κελευσθέντες modifies the soldiers (the subject of ἦλθον), and that the genitive phrase identifies those in power who gave the order.
rejected: those ordered by this wretched and fleeting life
the ones commanded by this miserable and flowing life

choices.term: νέος ὢν Λώτ, οὐ Σοδομιτῶν, ἀλλὰ Σινωπέων
choices.english: being a new Lot, not of the Sodomites, but of the Sinopeans
choices.why: Keeps the genitive of association with Lot and preserves the contrast between the two peoples.
rejected: a new Lot, not among Sodomites but among Sinopeans
being a second Lot, not of Sodom but of Sinope

bible_refs.method: ἐφρυάξαντο ἔθνη... καὶ οἱ βασιλεῖς καὶ οἱ ἄρχοντες συνήγοντο ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό
bible_refs.note: Quotes LXX Psalm 2:1 (Hebrew numbering Psalm 2:1); the author cites 'according to the psalmist' (κατὰ τὸν ψαλμῳδόν).

pass_b_english: The whole catalog of the noble martyrs is holy and divine, rendering grace for suffering through suffering, and fulfilling the repayment of blood to the Savior of all through blood. Yet even among these, not all share one glory, nor have equal honors been allotted to all by one measure; rather, first and second place do not escape even the catalog of the saints. The reason, I think, is the judge's very exact and impartial assessment. For he oversees both the magnitude of punishments and the steadfastness of endurance, and as he weighs the contest he distributes rewards to the athletes according to their worth. And it is not at all surprising if justice is honored this way by God, since even among us generals and contest judges do not treat all who excel or all who compete alike, but vote gifts proportionate to the measure of each one's achievement.

I have gone through all this to show that the one who today gives us the occasion for this gathering is more distinguished than his companions and fellow contestants. For the others are not all known everywhere, nor do they have a celebrated courage; but Phocas there is no one who does not know. Just as the sun's ray is spread before all eyes, so too the fame of this martyr has sounded in every ear. For as soon as I enter his honored shrine and touch the sacred tomb of his body, I am filled from the place itself with the memory of all the stories told about him. I see the gardener in his occupation, the simplicity of his soul, his hospitality, the extraordinary man of the coast, the benefactor of the inland region, and I become a disciple of the martyr by learning to keep devotion even to the final dangers.

But come, if it seems good, I will set aside what is common and known to many and tell you, who love the martyrs, the extraordinary stories of the martyr. This holy man, the great blessing of Christians, was brought forth by neighboring Sinope, an ancient and well-known city, rich in noble and philosophical men. His occupation in life was the cultivation and care of a garden, which he owned somewhere before the gate of the city at the mouth of the isthmus and worked diligently, providing comfort for his own life and for those in need. He also opened his small and poor hearth to strangers very eagerly. Dwelling beside the highway, he set out what he had as common property for those passing through; he was a new Lot, not of the Sodomites, but of the Sinopeans.

As time went on, he found the commandment not without reward; for from his hospitality he gained the occasion for his life-giving death. Hear now, taking up the story briefly, from where and how it happened. When the word of our devotion was proclaimed and the wondrous preaching went out to every ear, making Christ known and the mysteries that come from him, the nations raged, according to the psalmist, and the kings and rulers gathered together (Psalm 2:1–2; cf. Acts 4:25–26). And the peoples of error were angry that Jesus had become king. Every Christian was sought as a criminal, and the one nearby was punished while the one far away was hunted down. Therefore not even the lowliness of his occupation or his gardening hid Phocas, but he too was denounced as a genuine initiate of Christ. And so those who had been ordered to end this wretched and fleeting life came against him.

problems.quote: those who had been ordered by the rulers of this wretched and fleeting life
problems.source_quote: οἱ τοῦ δυστήνου τοῦδε βίου καὶ ῥέοντος κελευσθέντες
problems.why: "κελευσθέντες" modifies the soldiers (those ordered), but "τοῦ δυστήνου τοῦδε βίου καὶ ῥέοντος" describes the life, not rulers; no "rulers" in source.
problems.fix: those ordered to deal with this wretched and fleeting life
problems.ruling: No word for 'rulers' in source; τοῦ δυστήνου τοῦδε βίου describes 'life,' not rulers.

problems.source_quote: ἐφρυάξαντο ἔθνη, κατὰ τὸν ψαλμῳδόν, καὶ οἱ βασιλεῖς καὶ οἱ ἄρχοντες συνήγοντο ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό
problems.why: The LXX of Psalm 2:1 reads "Ἐφρύαξαν ἔθνη καὶ λαοὶ ἐμελέτησαν κενά"—the quoted words match Acts 4:25-26 more closely than Ps 2:1 LXX.
problems.ruling: LXX Ps 2:1 differs; quoted wording better matches Acts 4:25-26, misleading reference.

edits.old: those who had been ordered by the rulers of this wretched and fleeting life
edits.new: those who had been ordered to deal with this wretched and fleeting life

fixed: mistranslation: source has no 'rulers'; 'κελευσθέντες' modifies the soldiers, and 'τοῦ δυστήνου τοῦδε βίου καὶ ῥέοντος' describes the life. Changed to 'those who had been ordered to deal with this wretched and fleeting life'.
wrong_scripture: the quoted words match Acts 4:25–26 more closely than Psalm 2:1 LXX; updated citation to '(Psalm 2:1–2; cf. Acts 4:25–26)'.

problems.quote: for from his hospitality he gained the occasion of the life-giving death
problems.source_quote: ἀπὸ γὰρ τῆς φιλοξενίας ἐκέρδανε τοῦ ζωοποιοῦ θανάτου τὴν πρόφασιν
problems.why: θανάτου is genitive dependent on πρόφασιν: 'pretext/occasion FOR death'. English reads as if death is life-giving, not that death gives life.
problems.fix: for from his hospitality he gained the occasion for his life-giving death
problems.ruling: Greek has πρόφασιν τοῦ θανάτου ('pretext for death'), not 'occasion of the life-giving death'; English misattributes ζωοποιοῦ to death rather than to implied resurrection life

edits.old: for from his hospitality he gained the occasion of the life-giving death
edits.new: for from his hospitality he gained the occasion for his life-giving death

fixed: Corrected 'occasion of the life-giving death' to 'occasion for his life-giving death' because θανάτου is genitive dependent on πρόφασιν, meaning 'occasion for death'; the death is life-giving, not the occasion.

problems.quote: for by suffering they returned grace on behalf of suffering, and by blood they fulfilled the repayment on behalf of blood to the Savior of all
problems.source_quote: πάθει τὴν ὑπὲρ πάθους ἀποδοὺς χάριν, αἵματι δὲ τὴν ὑπὲρ αἵματος τῷ Σωτῆρι τῶν ὅλων ἀμοιβὴν ἐκπληρώσας
problems.why: Subject is the catalog (singular), not 'they'; grace is owed to martyrs, not returned by them.
problems.fix: rendering grace for suffering through suffering, and fulfilling the repayment of blood to the Savior of all through blood
problems.ruling: Subject is singular κατάλογος (catalog), not 'they'; ἀποδοὺς/ἐκπληρώσας are singular participles modifying it. Also 'returned grace' reverses direction: martyrs receive grace from God, not return it.

problems.quote: those who had been ordered to deal with this wretched and fleeting life
problems.source_quote: οἱ τοῦ δυστήνου τοῦδε βίου καὶ ῥέοντος κελευσθέντες
problems.why: Missing object: ordered to do WHAT? Source implies 'ordered [to take his life]' or 'executioners'; 'deal with' is vague and misleading
problems.fix: those ordered to [end] this wretched and fleeting life
problems.ruling: κελευσθέντες lacks explicit object; 'deal with' is vague. Source implies ordered to seize/execute Phocas; reader misled.

edits.old: for by suffering they returned grace on behalf of suffering, and by blood they fulfilled the repayment on behalf of blood to the Savior of all
edits.new: rendering grace for suffering through suffering, and fulfilling the repayment of blood to the Savior of all through blood

edits.old: those who had been ordered to deal with this wretched and fleeting life
edits.new: those who had been ordered to end this wretched and fleeting life

fixed: The first problem is real: the source has a singular subject (the catalog) and the grace is rendered to the martyrs, not returned by them. The edit fixes the meaning while keeping the English literary.
The second problem is real: the source implies the soldiers were ordered to take Phocas's life, and 'deal with' is too vague. The edit supplies the missing object.

dismissed.why: The work brief states Psalms should use Hebrew numbering with note where LXX differs. The source cites 'according to the psalmist' without specifying Psalm 2. The English adds Psalm 2:1-2 and Acts 4:25-26 without noting this is LXX Psalm 2 = Hebrew Psalm 2 (same here, but the procedure is violated by not noting the LXX basis). More critically, the source has no 'cf. Acts'—the English adds this cross-reference.
dismissed.note: Psalm 2 has the same number in the Septuagint and the Hebrew. Supplying a reference for 'the psalmist' and a cf. to Acts 4:25–26, which uses the same wording, is normal editorial practice.
